core_obligations: Use the localized-site description (proof lines 4359-4360): the equality H^q(U, K) = H^q(C/U, K|_{C/U}) holds by the same-chapter result, so the presheaf to be sheafified is the one in the statement.
Compute the presheaf on a K-injective representative (proof lines 4361-4367): choosing I^bullet representing K, one has H^q(U, K) = ker(I^q(U) -> I^{q+1}(U)) / im(I^{q-1}(U) -> I^q(U)).

Identify the sheafification (proof lines 4368-4370): since H^q(K) is by definition ker(I^q -> I^{q+1}) / im(I^{q-1} -> I^q), the presheaf displayed is the presheaf of sections of H^q(K), whose sheafification is H^q(K) itself.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite H^q(U, K) using the localized site.
Choose a K-injective representative and write the presheaf as kernel modulo image of its section complex.
Recognise this presheaf as the presheaf of sections of the cohomology sheaf.
Its sheafification is therefore the cohomology sheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the sheafification of the presheaf U -> H^q(U, K) with the cohomology sheaf H^q(K) (statement lines 4348-4356). The proof is a short but genuine computation: after rewriting H^q(U, K) through the localized site, one chooses a K-injective representative I^bullet so that the presheaf becomes the presheaf of kernels modulo images of the section complex, which is exactly the presheaf of sections of the cohomology sheaf H^q(K), so its sheafification is H^q(K) (proof lines 4359-4370). The claim is H2: one representative choice and one comparison of presheaves.
